_comment: LINEDOWN — platform Qualified Vendor List (QVL) for AI-SRV-G4, memory subsystem only.
PURPOSE: this file makes the beat-4 Engineering BLOCK a real lookup, not a hardcoded string.
A QVL records what was TESTED on this platform. It is not a compatibility list. A module can
match every electrical requirement in `requirements` and still be correctly blocked, because
nobody has ever run 24 of them in this board at full thermal load. That is the whole point of
beat 4 and it is the truthful engineering position.
KEY SHAPE: `platform`, `platformLabel`, `qualified[]`, `approvedAlternates[]`, `requirements{}`
are the contract agreed with the AGENTS track (qualification engine parses these). Everything
else is additive context and safe to ignore.
LOOKUP SEMANTICS: exact MPN present in `qualified` or `approvedAlternates` with status
'qualified' => PASS. Not present in either => BLOCK, even if specs match `requirements`
exactly. Check `evaluationQueue[]` on a miss for the richer reason (submitted but untested).
Entries with status 'withdrawn' are NOT a pass. 'qualified-conditional' requires every item in
its `conditions` to hold.
MODULE vs DIE — read before writing any reason string: every entry describes a complete 288-pin
RDIMM ASSEMBLY. `dieRevision` is a descriptor of the as-validated module build (it records
which build was on the bench), NOT a substitutable attribute. Sourcing an alternate here means
buying a different complete module from a different module manufacturer. It NEVER means
substituting DRAM die inside a module. Do not generate text that implies otherwise.
AUTHENTICITY IS A SEPARATE CHECK: a qualified MPN offered by a non-franchised broker still
passes this QVL. QVL answers 'was this part tested here'. It does not answer 'is this physical
module genuine'. That is the marking/counterfeit check in data/markings/. Beats 4 and 5 are two
orthogonal findings on purpose.
Validation report IDs, BIOS versions, dates and EVAL IDs are illustrative.

platformDetail.populationRule: 1DPC, all 24 slots populated, single MPN per node — no mixed-vendor population within a node
platformDetail.airflowEnvelope: 35C inlet nominal / 45C short-term excursion, 70C module case worst case hot-aisle

requirementsDetail.note: These are the five fields the qualification engine compares field-by-field on an MPN miss, plus the detail fields recorded for the audit trail.

policy.rationale: Spec compatibility is not qualification. A module may satisfy every entry in `requirements` and still be blocked: qualification is evidence that THIS module build was run in THIS board at full 24-slot loading across the thermal envelope. Absent a validation report, the platform owner cannot stand behind the configuration.
policy.plain: Only memory that has actually been tested in this exact server is allowed. Matching the spec sheet is not enough.
policy.escalationPath: Platform Engineering memory owner may grant a deviation only with a completed margin report plus a signed customer-notified deviation record. No deviation was granted in this run.

qualified.notes: Incumbent. Allocation cut 40% on 2026-10-03 — this is the shortage that opened the run. Part remains qualified; supply, not qualification, is the problem.
32GB SKU. Qualified for the G4 board but NOT a substitute on this program — AI-SRV-G4 is specified at 1.5TB per node and there is no second DIMM per channel to make up the capacity.

approvedAlternates.role: qualified alternate — promoted to primary alternate by commit 7f3c1ab (rev-E)
testCoverage: margin shmoo: VDDQ / tRCD / RTT at 4800 MT/s
thermal soak to 70C module case, no throttle, no CE escalation
SPD5 hub and PMIC telemetry readback via BMC
approvedAlternates.notes: THE APPROVED WINNER of this run. Mechanically and electrically a drop-in module replacement for the Micron incumbent: same 288-pin RDIMM, 31.25mm, 2Rx4, same 1DPC population rules, no board change, no BIOS change, no die substitution.

Fully qualified. Rejected in this run on SCHEDULE ONLY — 14-week factory lead time against an 11-day kit date, no franchised or bonded stock located. Nothing wrong with the part. Keep this distinction in any narration: a schedule reject is not a quality reject.

Module-house alternate, qualified. Not quoted in this run — no stock at the franchised distributor on the 11-day window. Present in the file so the lookup has depth and so the demo can survive a question about third sources.

conditions: requires BIOS G4-BIOS-1.4.0 or later — program is shipping 1.3.2
down-bins to 4800 MT/s on this platform; the 5600 rating is not realised
changes node capacity to 2.3TB — requires a customer-approved configuration change
whole-node population only, no partial mix with 64GB modules
approvedAlternates.notes: Not viable in this run: the program is frozen on BIOS 1.3.2 and the capacity change needs customer sign-off. Included because 'why not just use the bigger one' is the obvious audience question and the file should answer it.

approvedAlternates.withdrawnReason: SPD5 hub thermal-sensor readback erratum under 24-slot loading; superseded by HMCG94MEBRA109N (report MV-G4-0291). Specs match `requirements` exactly and this entry MUST still fail the lookup.
approvedAlternates.notes: Deliberate trap for the qualification engine: an exact MPN hit that is NOT a pass. Verify the engine checks `status`, not just presence.

evaluationQueue.specCompareToRequirements: MATCH on all five fields (capacityGB, speedMTps, ranks, formFactor, voltage)
testsPassed: single-module POST and boot on ASRV-G4-MB-C2
testsOutstanding: thermal soak to 70C module case — never run
margin shmoo at 4800 MT/s (VDDQ / tRCD / RTT) — never run
BMC PMIC/hub telemetry readback — never run
evaluationQueue.blockingReason: No RDIMM validation report issued. Thermal margin and 24-slot loading tests never completed — samples returned to the vendor 2026-08-09 when the chamber slot was reassigned to the 96GB SKU.
evaluationQueue.plain: This supplier sent samples in July. Testing was started and never finished, so there is no report. On paper the part is an exact match for what the server needs — but nobody has ever run 24 of them in one machine at full load.
evaluationQueue.notes: THE BEAT-4 BLOCK TARGET. Absent from `qualified` and `approvedAlternates` by design, and spec-compatible on every field by design, so the block cannot be dismissed as 'wrong part'. It is the strongest form of the beat: electrically fine, commercially cheapest, still blocked, because QVL records what was tested and not what fits.
evaluationQueue.pathToQualification: Supply 40 modules plus a thermal chamber slot; ~6 weeks to a signed report. Re-quote next program phase.

evaluationQueue.blockingReason: Vendor withdrew samples before thermal soak. No report.
evaluationQueue.plain: Another supplier that started the approval process and did not finish it.
evaluationQueue.notes: Depth only. Not quoted in this run. Illustrative MPN.

approvedChannels: franchised/authorised distributor with certificate of conformance and manufacturer traceability

blacklist.reason: Remarked modules offered as MTC20F2085S1RC48BA1. Six independent top-marking failures confirmed; see data/markings/. Filed to ERAI.
blacklist.plain: Banned supplier. They sold us relabelled memory pretending to be a part we use.
blacklist.note: IMPORTANT: the MPN they offered IS on this QVL. The QVL lookup passes. Authenticity is a separate check and that is why this is a second, independent beat.

changeLog.summary: Baseline for this run. Micron incumbent + Samsung / SK hynix / Kingston alternates; HMCG94AGBRA109N withdrawn; 96GB SKU qualified-conditional.

Promote M321R8GA0BB0-CQK to qualified primary alternate (MV-G4-0288). Record Engineering block of TRA564G48D436O (EVAL-G4-0412 incomplete). Record schedule rejection of HMCG94MEBRA109N (14-week lead). Blacklist broker lot PRC-24817. Attach PO-4471982.
